correctness.rationale: Enumeration of all 710 nonempty simplices (20,130,320,240) and signed boundaries. Exact unit-pivot integer reductions give SNF(d1)=1^19, SNF(d2)=1^111, SNF(d3)=1^208,2, with residual rank-one minors and gcd two checked; chain condition verified. Therefore the claimed integral homology holds. Exhaustive signed Lefschetz traces on all 14 S5 x C2 conjugacy classes, independently reconstructed using rim-hook characters, prove the Specht decomposition; embedded standard-library scripts replay both computations.

value.rationale: The bidirected biclique is a natural symmetric family in multipath-complex topology; n=5 is the first new case beyond the previously computed torsion onset. It has a qualitatively different integral homological profile (2-torsion in degree two together with rank 31 in degree three). Determining its complete S5 x C2 homology representation distinguishes two 16/15-dimensional symmetry sectors, no leaf-invariant classes, and explicit irreducible constituents invisible to Betti numbers. This is more than an unmotivated next-rank computation.
